A fixed-size array emulates rows and columns; pupils[row,column] identifies one cell using zero-based indexes.

m.title: Two-Dimensional Arrays and Records
m.q: Use the Pupils table: ID 101 Ada 72; ID 102 Ben 43; ID 103 Mia 81. In the string-based 2D array, what is pupils[0,1]? Explain the two indexes.
st: Label rows 0, 1 and 2 for Ada, Ben and Mia. Columns 0, 1 and 2 hold ID, Name and Mark.
The FIRST index 0 selects Ada's record (row 0), not column 0.
The SECOND index 1 selects the Name field (column 1).
pupils[0,1] is 'Ada'. Both indexes start at 0; marks are represented as text in this particular array.

k.q: Predict the name printed. The array has three rows and three columns; only the Name column is initialised here.
k.code:
array pupils[3,3]
pupils[0,1] = "Ada"
pupils[1,1] = "Ben"
pupils[2,1] = "Mia"
print(pupils[1,1])
p: Explain your predicted result using the first assignment or test.
Change the final indexes to [2,1]. Predict the new output.
Identify why pupils[3,1] is out of bounds; then assign '72' to pupils[0,2] and explain why the quotes matter.
k.a: Ben; then Mia. Row 3 is outside indexes 0–2. '72' is stored as text in a string-based table; numeric comparisons require conversion or a numeric structure.

e: In the Pupils table, state the Name stored at row index 1, column index 1. [2 marks]
Ben [1]; the first index selects row 1 and the second index selects Name/column 1 [1].
Explain what a row (record) and a column (field) represent in the Pupils table. [4 marks]
A row stores the data for one pupil [1] across that pupil's related values [1]. A field/column stores the same property, such as Mark [1], for all pupil records [1].
Describe one difference between a 2D array of text and a named pupil record. [3 marks]
The 2D array is accessed by row and column indexes [1] and uses one consistent element type [1]; a named record uses field names and may store different field types [1].
v: A 2D array stores values in rows and columns and can be accessed with two indexes.
In a zero-indexed grid, the first row and column use index 0.
A record groups related fields about one entity under a single item.
Use a grid for table-like values and a record for named fields such as name and age.
x: A 2D array uses two indexes to locate an element.
r: State the difference between concatenation and arithmetic addition.
Concatenation joins string content; arithmetic addition calculates a numerical sum.
State the difference between RAM and ROM.
RAM is volatile working memory; ROM stores persistent firmware.
Give the array after one pass of bubble sort on [3,1,2].

mastery.task: Represent the same Pupils data using named records with a text Name and integer Mark. Write an algorithm that outputs the names of pupils with a mark of at least 50.
mastery.hint: A record may have differently typed fields. For each pupil, IF pupil.Mark >= 50 THEN print(pupil.Name).
mastery.answer: Records: (101,'Ada',72), (102,'Ben',43), (103,'Mia',81). Iterate records; only Ada and Mia satisfy Mark >= 50. Explain that this is different from comparing text strings.
